content: KeyDB (docs.keydb.dev + GitHub wiki): Redis-compatible multithreaded fork; active-replica / multiple-masters modes let all instances accept writes concurrently (no Sentinel needed). Limitations: asynchronous replication with NO conflict resolution or CRDTs - two nodes writing the same key resolve last-replicated-write-wins nondeterministically; on link drop both sides keep writing and diverge in key state; cluster spec says last failover wins. Community (valkey #512) contrasts it with proper CRDT active-active. Also: FLASH storage tier (~85% RAM throughput, +0.5ms), subkey expires.
